$Comment: Quartermaster Bramble, the Emerald Wilds supply giver, standing beside a Kweebec merchant post.
Where: the world named 'default', which is the persistent world players log into, never an
instance - a bare word under Match is an exact name. If your server's main world has another
name, change it here (or override this placement by id from your own pack).
Anchor.Structure attaches the placement to a worldgen spawn marker, so Bramble lands at a post
the world actually generated. MarkerIds is an exact, case-insensitive allow-list; run
/mmonpc structures in game to see the marker ids a world has loaded before authoring one, and
note that the allow-list is FAIL-CLOSED, so a typo means Bramble never appears at all.
Limits: one per world, and every matching marker is used. Raise MaxPerWorld to stand one at
every matching post instead.
Identity.Role names the NPC role this placement spawns. Bramble's look and nameplate live in
that role file (Server/NPC/Roles/Passive/Quartermaster_Wilds.json), which this pack ships, so
re-dress him there rather than here. Point Role at a different role id to stand somebody else
at the posts.
This placement authors no Identity.NpcId, so the character IS its role: the pack's quests
name Quartermaster_Wilds as their npcViewId, the dialogue destination below carries it, and a talk step
credits against it. Author an NpcId to make this standing a character of its own that
nothing else answers to.
Press F opens Bramble's dialogue, authored as a ui_target rather than as Interact.Dialogue so
the character id travels with it. That id is what the dialogue's own 'npcquests:@self' options resolve
against and what puts the character's name in the header; it is also what the pack's quests bind
as their npcViewId.
Name: Quartermaster_Wilds
